10. After investigation, the police has filed a chargesheet against Respondent no.1.

In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
11. In the present case, the driver and the owner of the offending vehicle have neither filed their written statement nor cross-examined PW-1.
To rebut the claim of the petitioner they have not led any evidence in their defence.

It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him.
Thus, it stands proved that the petitioner suffered injuries in road traffic accident due to rash CHARU

In totality of circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner has been able to prove on the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offen
Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
Since it stands proved that the accident occurred due to rashness and negligence of Respondent no.1, Respondent no.2/owner of offending vehicle is vicariously liable.

Further, as offending vehicle is not insured, both Respondents are liable to compensate the petitioner.
14.

As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors.
(2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680.
The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

15.1. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a)
and (iv).
Decisions of Hon'ble SC and Hon'ble High Courts contain necessary guidelines for award under these heads, if necessary.

15.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a).
We are not concerned with assessment regarding loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability in this case, as petitioner did not suffer any permanent disability.
16. As per record, date of birth of petitioner is 15.02.1984.
Same has not been disputed.
Accident occurred on 14.01.2020.
As such, petitioner would have been about 36 years at the time of accident.

As per discharge note Ex.PW-1/6, injured suffered fracture of both bone and after PAC clearance,
patient was operated.
Thus, keeping note of the fact that the petitioner suffered a fracture, it has to be treated as grievous injury.
No medical bills have been filed on record.

As regards loss of earning of petitioner, it first needs to be ascertained as to what was the nature of job and salary/wages drawn by petitioner at the time of accident.
Petitioner has claimed to be working in private company and getting salary of Rs.21,000/-p.m., however no evidence has been lead to prove his employment or salary.

As petitioner has neither placed any record his educational qualification or proof of employment, his monthly income is taken on the basis of minimum wages of un- skilled labour of Delhi of the year 2020 is taken.
Same is Rs.14,842/-.
Having regard to the documents on record and the nature of injury suffered, it is assumed that the petitioner may have been incapacitated from working for at least three months.
Accordingly, petitioner is entitled to compensation towards loss of income for three months.
As such, loss of income would have been taken as Rs.14,842/-X3=Rs.44,526/-, accordingly granted.
He is also entitled to attendant charges for the said period.
